approachQuestion.prompt:
Compatible Table Labels

Assign a label in {0,...,k-1} to each vertex of an undirected simple graph. Adjacent vertices must have different labels. Return every valid length-n label vector, once. Label names are meaningful: globally swapping two labels produces a different answer.

Examples:
n=2, adjacency=[[false,true],[true,false]], k=2 -> [[0,1],[1,0]].
n=3, adjacency=[[false,true,true],[true,false,true],[true,true,false]], k=2 -> [].

Constraints: 1 <= n <= 12; 1 <= k <= 4. Input is an n by n symmetric boolean adjacency matrix with false diagonal.

options.text: Assign vertices in order, try every label, and reject a choice when it equals the label of an already assigned neighbor. Restore the current assignment before trying another label.
options.feedback: Every edge is checked when its later endpoint is assigned. Rejected prefixes cannot extend to a valid vector, while each valid vector follows one branch.

options.text: Choose the smallest currently legal label for each vertex and never reconsider it.
options.feedback: A greedy choice can dead-end despite a solution: in order 0,1,2,3, edges [(0,2),(2,3),(3,1)] and k=2, the first two greedy labels are both 0, forcing both endpoints of edge (2,3) to 1.

options.text: Always fix vertex 0 to label 0 to remove equivalent global renamings.
options.feedback: Renamings are distinct required answers. The n=2 example needs [1,0] as well as [0,1].

options.text: Generate every full label vector and check all matrix entries only after the vector is complete.
options.feedback: This returns the exact answers, but keeps extending prefixes with an already violated edge; checking assigned neighbors removes that work.

feedback.reason: Every edge is checked when its later endpoint is assigned. Rejected prefixes cannot extend to a valid vector, while each valid vector follows one branch.
details: Assign vertices in numeric order. At vertex i try all k labels; scan vertices 0 through i-1 using the matrix, and recurse only if no assigned neighbor has that label. Undo the assignment. Copy complete vectors.

Before assigning vertex i, check only already assigned neighbors. Undo its label after the branch. Testing merely the previous vertex misses conflicts with earlier nonadjacent-in-order vertices connected in the graph.

Restore the current assignment before trying another label.”: Every edge is checked when its later endpoint is assigned. complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze `acm-b18-06-search` only. Let C be the total number of earlier-vertex matrix entries actually examined across all candidate-label trials, V the number of recursive calls, and R the number of label entries copied into output. Initialize an n-entry assignment array. A neighbor scan may stop at its first conflict. Choose the tightest stated time and auxiliary-space pair. Count recursion and mutable working state; exclude supplied input and returned output storage, but include copying work in time. Primitive integer/index operations and preallocated-array updates cost constant time; dynamic appends are amortized constant time. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(n + V + C + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n + V + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n + V + C + R) time, O(n²) auxiliary space
O(n² + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Count actual adjacency checks across bounded label trials and copied assignments.
details: At most four labels are tried per call, contributing constant overhead per call; C accounts for actual scans, and copying adds R. Initialization adds n.
The assignment array and depth-n stack are linear; the matrix is supplied input.

Let C be the total number of earlier-vertex matrix entries actually examined across all candidate-label trials, V the number of recursive calls, and R the number of label entries copied into output. Initialize an n-entry assignment array. A neighbor scan may stop at its first conflict.
“O(n + V + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: A trial can scan many earlier vertices, which is counted by C.
“O(n + V + C + R) time, O(n²) auxiliary space”: The adjacency matrix belongs to the supplied input.
“O(n² + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Enumerating many valid assignments requires a potentially exponential search.
